title: ATLAHS: An Application-centric Network Simulator Toolchain for AI, HPC, and Distributed Storage
problem: Existing network simulators rely on synthetic microbenchmarks or are domain-specific, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive performance insights for realistic AI, HPC, and storage workloads.
motivation: Accurate simulation of real-world communication patterns enables better hardware design decisions and system optimization for emerging AI systems, large-scale HPC, and distributed storage.
method: Introduce ATLAHS, a flexible, open-source simulation toolchain that traces real applications and simulates their workloads using the Group Operation Assembly Language (GOAL) format. Support multiple simulation backends and multi-job/multi-tenant scenarios.
key_novelty: GOAL-based trace format for portable workload representation; application-centric simulation supporting AI, HPC, and storage; demonstrated accuracy with <5% error; outperforms AstraSim in runtime and efficiency.
contributions: ATLAHS open-source simulation toolchain for realistic workload modeling
GOAL format for portable application trace representation
Less than 5% simulation error on realistic workloads

metrics.comparison: outperforms AstraSim in runtime and trace size

limitations: Specific case study results not detailed in abstract; accuracy validation methodology not clear; scalability to petabyte-scale trace files not discussed.
